title: What a Governor Can and Can't Do

endcard.line: Pictures: juggadery (CC BY 2.0); David Castor (public domain)

left.title: Can
items: reserve a bill for the President

right.title: Usually can't
items: except where the Constitution allows discretion

segments.say: A Governor is the head of a State. But how much can a Governor actually do on their own?
The President appoints a Governor by warrant, for five years, at the President's pleasure. The minimum age is thirty-five.
One person can even be Governor of two or more States at once.
Under Article one sixty-three, a Council of Ministers led by the Chief Minister aids and advises the Governor, except where the Constitution requires the Governor to act in discretion.
When a bill passed by the State legislature arrives, the Governor can assent, withhold assent, return it for another look unless it's a Money Bill, or reserve it for the President.

anim.title: Two more powers
items: Ordinances when the legislature isn't sitting (Article 213)
A report that can lead to President's rule (Article 356)

segments.say: The Governor can issue ordinances when the legislature is not sitting, and can send the report that may lead to President's rule under Article three fifty-six.
For GS Two, read Articles one sixty-three and two hundred most closely. That is where the Governor's real limits are drawn.

sources: Constitution of India, official English text (Legislative Department diglot PDF, legislative.gov.in, 'as on' 2024 edition): Art. 153 (a Governor for each State; one person may be Governor of two or more States); Art. 155 (appointed by the President by warrant); Art. 156 (holds office during the pleasure of the President; term of five years); Art. 157 (citizen of India, at least thirty-five years of age); Art. 163 (Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at the head to aid and advise, except where the Governor is required to act in discretion); Art. 200 (assent, withhold, reserve for the President, or return a Bill other than a Money Bill); Art. 213 (ordinances when the Legislature is not in session); Art. 356 (President's rule on a report from the Governor or otherwise)

quiz.q: What is the minimum age to be appointed Governor?
quiz.why: Art. 157: a citizen who has completed thirty-five years.

quiz.q: Which bill can a Governor NOT return to the legislature for reconsideration?
quiz.why: Art. 200: the return option is for a Bill other than a Money Bill.

quiz.q: Who aids and advises the Governor under Article 163?
options: The Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister
quiz.why: Art. 163: the Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at the head.
